chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What is your ruling regarding a man who struck a young woman on her abdomen, injuring her womb and disrupting her menstruation, and she stated that her menstruation had ceased because of that, while her menstruation had previously been regular?

He عليه السلام said: “She is to be observed for one year. If her womb recovers and her menstruation returns to what it was, otherwise she is to take an oath, and the one who struck her must pay one-third of her diyyah for the damage to her womb and the cessation of her menstruation.”

key_terms.ارْتِفَاعِ طَمْثِهَا: cessation of her menstruation; the loss resulting from the injury
key_terms.اسْتُحْلِفَتْ: she is made to take an oath to confirm the continuing injury
key_terms.ثُلُثَ دِيَتِهَا: one-third of her blood money; the compensation imposed in this case
key_terms.رَحِمَهَا: her womb; the organ whose injury is the basis of legal liability here
key_terms.طَمْثُهَا: her menstruation; the regular menstrual flow discussed in the ruling
key_terms.فَسَادِ رَحِمِهَا: damage to her womb; the lasting bodily harm being compensated

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if striking a woman causes damage to her womb and stops her menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on bodily injury inflicted upon a woman that causes damage to her womb and the cessation of menstruation. The Imam عليه السلام orders a waiting period of one year to assess recovery; if the harm remains, the woman swears an oath and the assailant is held financially liable for one-third of her diyyah.
